name: North Adelaide
reason: Suburb wrapper: Wikivoyage's North Adelaide entries are dining streets and separate sights (St Peter's, Montefiore Hill); no distinct thing to see under this name. Searched Wikivoyage and SATC.

name: North Terrace
reason: A boulevard that wraps its own institutions (Art Gallery, SA Museum, Migration Museum, Botanic Garden), each a spot; SATC and Wikivoyage describe it only by listing them. Part of larger spots.

name: State Library of South Australia
reason: For: two SATC pages name it, free, heritage Mortlock Chamber and Treasures Wall exhibitions open daily. Against: a library is a civic building by the rules (Turanga benchmark); the draw is a reading room and a small display, ~30 min.

name: St Francis Xavier's Cathedral
reason: For: Wikivoyage lists it open daily 7-7, free, 'rather impressive ... particularly on the inside'. Against: single source, no named art or architecture beyond that; a city-centre church by Victoria Square. Searched for a second counted source, found none.

name: Australian Space Discovery Centre
reason: Free public Space Gallery at Lot Fourteen with hands-on exhibits; named by Wikivoyage, SATC and Experience Adelaide (three counted sources). Permanent museum-style exhibit, 30-60 min.

name: Adelaide Holocaust Museum
reason: Wikivoyage lists it with hours (Sun, Tue-Thu; booking on Tue-Thu), $10; a permanent small museum open to the public. Second-tier museum a guide names. Case against: limited days, bookings, single source.

name: Adelaide Town Hall
reason: For: SATC lists volunteer public tours of the heritage hall and organ, 'one of Adelaide's icons'. Against: a civic building visited only by scheduled tour, and the SATC page gives no schedule; one counted source.

name: Old Parliament House
reason: Duplicate of Parliament House: the free public tours of Parliament House on North Terrace cover the original 1850s chamber in the old building. No separate counted visitor listing found (searched SATC, Wikivoyage, parliament.sa.gov.au).

name: Parliament House
reason: The Parliament of South Australia (managing agency) runs free public tours, no booking, twice daily on non-sitting days, covering the 1850s chamber, House of Assembly and Legislative Council; open to the public inside. Case against: civic building, tour-only; no SATC listing found.

name: Victoria Square
reason: City of Adelaide's visitor site (Experience Adelaide) features Victoria Square / Tarntanyangga as the central square: Three Rivers fountain, Kaurna significance, birthplace of the Aboriginal flag. Permanent, free. Case against: a square, ~20 min.

name: Chinatown, Adelaide
reason: Wikivoyage lists only a pedestrian strip (Moonta St) beside Central Market; a dining strip with nothing to see or do of its own. Searched Wikivoyage and Experience Adelaide.

name: Ayers House
reason: Closed: the National Trust museum closed on 26 Sept 2021 after eviction; no counted source found listing it as open (searched SATC and web).

name: Torrens Lake and Elder Park
reason: Experience Adelaide (City of Adelaide visitor site) names Elder Park with the 1882 rotunda, lake walking tracks and paddleboat hire; SATC lists the riverbank and Popeye landing. Permanent, free. Popeye cruises are the operator, not the spot.

name: Adelaide Himeji Garden
reason: Experience Adelaide features the free Japanese garden (rock-and-sand and lake gardens, teahouse, stepping stones) in the south Park Lands, open daily. Case against: small, ~30 min.

name: Veale Gardens
reason: Experience Adelaide lists Veale Gardens: formal serpentine canal, statues and the adjacent Adelaide-Qingdao Rose Garden, with guided walks on SATC. Permanent, free. Case against: ordinary Park Lands garden.

name: Botanic Park
reason: No dedicated visitor listing found (searched Experience Adelaide, SATC, Wikivoyage); only mentioned within a guided walk with the Botanic Garden; Sunday speakers' corner is a weekly event; adjoins the Zoo and Botanic Garden.

name: Rymill Park
reason: Experience Adelaide lists a duck lake and playground, and it hosts the Fringe; an ordinary Park Lands park with nothing distinct to see (ordinary-park benchmark).

name: West Terrace Cemetery
reason: SATC lists Adelaide Cemetery Tours of this State heritage cemetery; the Adelaide Cemeteries Authority offers 7-day self-guided interpretive trails (about an hour) plus guided tours. Case against: cemetery; some visit by tour.

name: JamFactory
reason: SATC lists JamFactory's studios and galleries (ceramics, glass, furniture, jewellery) with workshop tours; visitors can see makers at work and free gallery shows. Case against: part shop and a not-for-profit studio.

name: Beaumont House
reason: Rule 4: National Trust house open only on one Sunday afternoon a month (tours 2-4.30pm) or by arrangement; the SATC listing is an event ('open days').

name: Penfolds Magill Estate
reason: The SATC listing is for the Magill Estate Restaurant (dinner Wed-Sat, lunch weekends, 54 seats); a restaurant and cellar door, not a visitor place. No guide singles out the estate as an attraction.

name: Coopers Brewery
reason: Wikivoyage names the brewery tour and SATC lists the tours; Coopers runs a Visitor Centre tour and 90-min Brew Tour Tue-Sat. A famous brewery tour, the case COVERAGE allows. Against: a business, tours must be booked.

name: The Old Gum Tree
reason: For: SATC lists Old Gum Tree Reserve and the council describes it as where South Australia's colony was proclaimed on 28 Dec 1836. Against: a small reserve with a tree and plaques, a ten-minute look; close to the minor-memorial rule.

name: Army Museum of South Australia
reason: Wikivoyage lists the volunteer-run military museum (guns, artillery, WWI/WWII/Korea/Vietnam), $5; permanent museum a guide names. Case against: limited hours (Sun, Mon, Wed), one source.

name: Port Adelaide Lighthouse
reason: Part of the South Australian Maritime Museum precinct (an exhibit of the museum) and seen from outside; 10-minute look. Wikivoyage is the only counted source; SATC only has it inside a museum tour.

name: Port Adelaide Historical Society Museum
reason: SATC lists the local community museum with maritime collection (Keith Leleu), models and audio-visual displays; permanent small museum a tourism board names. Case against: volunteer-run, one source.

name: Fishermen's Wharf Market
reason: Rule 4: a Sunday-only weekly market; searched SATC, Experience Adelaide and Wikivoyage, none lists it as an attraction.

name: Largs Bay
reason: City of Port Adelaide Enfield's visitor pages list the Largs Bay foreshore: 1882 jetty, kiosk, playground, walking paths, Largs Pier Hotel. A named beach and historic jetty. Council page was blocked to scripts (403); details from search. Against: no SATC listing.

name: Thompson Beach
reason: NPWS SA (parks.sa.gov.au) names Thompson Beach among the top spots to birdwatch in the Adelaide International Bird Sanctuary (migratory shorebirds Oct-Apr); Wikivoyage lists it too.

name: Glenelg Jetty
reason: Duplicate of Glenelg Beach: SATC's jetty page is a history blurb and Wikivoyage lists the jetty as part of Glenelg Beach, so it is the beach's own jetty.

name: Bay Discovery Centre
reason: Wikivoyage names the local-history museum in Glenelg Town Hall on Moseley Square. Permanent small museum a guide names. Case against: one source.

name: The Beachouse
reason: Wikivoyage lists this permanent seafront amusement park (mini-golf, carousel, bumper cars, mini train, slides); open daily. Against: a ticketed business.

name: Luna Park Glenelg
reason: Closed: a former amusement park (the Beachouse now occupies the site); no counted source lists it as open.

name: Brighton
reason: SATC's Adelaide beaches guide features Brighton: jetty, esplanade, Brighton Jetty Sculptures; Wikivoyage names the beach via the Seaford line. A second-tier beach.

name: Seacliff
reason: Only mentions found are accommodation listings (surf club, beach hotel) and the coastal trail; no counted source names the beach as a place to go (searched SATC, Wikivoyage, Experience Adelaide).

name: Marino Rocks Lighthouse
reason: Duplicate of Marino Conservation Park: the lighthouse is seen from the park's 1.2 km Botanical Trail; no counted source treats it as a separate visit.

name: Marino Conservation Park
reason: NPWS SA and SATC list the park: walking trail with views over Brighton, Glenelg and Marino Rocks Lighthouse, the last coastal heath on the Adelaide coast (Botanical Trail ~1.2 km).

name: Hallett Cove Beach
reason: Wikivoyage names the beaches at Hallett Cove and SATC's Hallett Cove Conservation Park page says the park's beach is popular for swimming; the Adelaide Coast Park Trail starts there. Note: shares the cove with Hallett Cove Conservation Park; merge if that is a spot.

name: Kingston Park Coastal Reserve
reason: SATC lists 'Kingston Park Coastal Reserve, Lookout and Aboriginal Tjilbruke Trail': cliff-top views over Holdfast Bay, Tjilbruke Spring, 76 indigenous plant species.

name: Port Noarlunga
reason: SATC lists Port Noarlunga Beach, Jetty, Reef and Aquatic Trail and its beaches guide singles out the reef as some of the best snorkelling in SA; jetty with stairs to the reef.

name: Christies Beach
reason: Only a grouped mention in SATC's beaches guide ('Port Noarlunga, Christies Beach and Moana ... explore the boardwalk'); no listing or feature of its own found (searched SATC, Wikivoyage).

name: Sturt Gorge Recreation Park
reason: NPWS SA lists the park: Sturt tillite glacial rocks, grey box woodland, new mountain-bike and hiking trails on the Craigburn Farm addition, waterholes along the Sturt River.

name: Warriparinga
reason: Living Kaurna Cultural Centre: SATC lists it, Marion council visitor page; guided one-hour cultural walk and heritage display on the Sturt wetlands.

name: Para Wirra Conservation Park
reason: Agency page names marked walks (Mack Creek Hike, Lake Discovery Walk), campground and wildlife.

name: Classic Jets Fighter Museum
reason: Wikivoyage See listing with description; aviation museum with cockpits to sit in, open most days; small museum, one counted source plus museum guides.

name: National Military Vehicle Museum
reason: Museum with running vehicles, open Sundays 10-4; named by Wikivoyage and History SA's Explore listing (counted heritage/visitor guide). Note: unconfirmed lease risk.

name: Tramway Museum, St Kilda
reason: Volunteer museum of 20+ trams with unlimited rides on a 1.6 km line to the St Kilda playground; History SA Explore and Salisbury council visitor listing. Open Sundays and holidays only (permanent venue, limited days).

name: St Kilda Mangrove Trail
reason: Case for: mangrove boardwalk long promoted by Salisbury council and DEW as a visit; birds and tidal wetlands, free. Case against: sources say the boardwalk is closed for maintenance until further notice after 2020 mangrove dieback (about 450 m open per a 2024 review) and needs a gate key; closed places fail.

name: Dazzeland
reason: Closed indoor amusement park (Myer Centre) that shut in 1998; no longer exists.

name: Greenhills Adventure Park
reason: Commercial adventure-park business; no counted source found by search; first pass also noted it lies in sa-fleurieu.

name: Waterfall Gully to Mount Lofty Summit Track
reason: Distinct, popular 3-4 hr climb past First and Second Falls to the summit; agency Cleland National Park page names the walk, plus walking guides. Part-of-larger risk is small: Mount Lofty Summit and Waterfall Gully are separate spots, the track is its own walk.

name: Mount Lofty Fire Tower
reason: Part of Mount Lofty Summit (tower stands on the summit); searched, no separate counted source.

name: Old Government House, Belair
reason: Case for: Wikivoyage names it in Belair NP, SA's first vice-regal summer residence, gold-coin entry, guided. Case against: open only the 1st and 3rd Sundays 1-4pm, so not there whenever a visitor arrives.

name: Kuitpo Forest
reason: Two counted sources: SATC Kuitpo walking trails page and ForestrySA walking page (Eucalypts Trail 1 hr, Tinjella, Chookarloo Walk). Some trails close for forestry operations.

name: Kenneth Stirling Conservation Park
reason: Searched parks.sa.gov.au and tourism sources: only walking blogs (weekendnotes, trailhiking) name its Filsell Hill and Wottons Scrub circuits; no counted source.

name: The Knoll Conservation Park
reason: Searched agency and tourism sources: no counted source found for a visitor draw.

name: Cudlee Creek Conservation Park
reason: 49 ha park, no visitor facilities, only Wikipedia and walker blogs; no counted source.

name: Yurrebilla Trail
reason: Regional tourism board walks page names the 54-56 km, three-day Belair-to-Chain-of-Ponds trail; SATC describes it too. Distinct named long walk (placement of a linear feature is decided later).

name: Heysen Trail
reason: SATC page for the 1,200 km Cape Jervis to Parachilna trail, suggesting sections near Adelaide for day walks; iconic. Linear feature, so place it at its main visitor access point.

name: Mawson Trail
reason: Case for: 900 km Adelaide-Blinman off-road cycle route, listed as a Tour Down Under Grand Tour and by Bike SA, famous with cyclists. Case against: I found no SATC or agency page; it is a cycling route spanning regions that starts at Athelstone, and a rider does not visit it for half an hour.

name: Lavender Federation Trail
reason: Long trail from Gawler to the Hills; searched, no counted source found.

name: Torrens Linear Park
reason: Suburban river path; no counted source found as a visitor draw.

name: Beerenberg Family Farm
reason: Wikivoyage See listing (entry fee, pick-your-own strawberries Nov-Apr) plus SATC page; two counted sources; seasonal venue is allowed.

name: Hahndorf Farm Barn
reason: Wikivoyage names the petting zoo with daily milking and animal handling, a 1-2 hr family stop; one counted source for an established attraction. Reported to have been listed for sale, so recheck it is operating.

name: Hahndorf Academy
reason: Free gallery and museum on Main Street (Peramangk, German settlers, 1900s classroom, Heysen sketches), open daily; Lonely Planet, SATC and History SA all name it.

name: Hahndorf Fairy Garden
reason: Small children's garden, one SATC source, minor stop of under 30 minutes.

name: Hahndorf Lavender Estate
reason: Working lavender farm and shop; one source, a commercial stop.

name: Crafers
reason: Village; only Wikivoyage mentions the Crafers Hotel under Sleep; no sight named.

name: Aldgate
reason: Village; Wikivoyage names only accommodation; no sight for a visitor.

name: Bridgewater
reason: Village; no counted source names a thing to see.

name: Stangate House and Garden
reason: Private/limited-access garden; no counted source found.

name: Mount Barker
reason: Service town; Wikivoyage names it only as a larger town. Its draws are a Saturday farmers market (event rule), wineries and Laratinga Wetlands, not named by a counted source.

name: Lobethal
reason: Wikivoyage names only the Lights of Lobethal (annual event); no permanent sight named. Its bushland park is judged separately.

name: Lobethal Bushland Park
reason: SATC page: reservoirs in stringybark forest with walking circuits, an hour or more.

name: Lobethal Archives and Historical Museum
reason: Small local-history museum; only Wikipedia found, no counted source.

name: Harben Vale Pick Your Own Cherries
reason: Seasonal commercial PYO farm; business.

name: Lenswood
reason: Orchard village; SATC lists only a PYO apples business; no distinct permanent place to see.

name: Jurlique Farm
reason: Case for: SATC lists the biodynamic rose and lavender farm and its tours; a recognised Hills visit. Case against: access appears to be paid guided tours only (about $280 with lunch), closed Sundays, so it is an operator experience rather than a place you can drop into.

name: Brayfield Park Lavender Farm
reason: Commercial lavender farm and shop; one source.

name: Norton Summit
reason: Village with pub and lookout; searched, only Wikipedia; no counted source.

name: Kanmantoo
reason: Former mining town; no counted source naming a public sight.

name: Eagle on the Hill
reason: Roadside hotel; Wikipedia only, no counted source.

name: Kaurna Trail
reason: Experience Adelaide (city tourism) lists the self-guided Kaurna heritage walk with art and stories; a permanent named route.
